title: Explicit scalar color maps, source-normal displacement and vector arrows

supportedProfile: Bounded scalar/vector expression sampling on an existing mesh vertex domain with explicit validity
Linear RGB stop maps with fixed or per-frame auto ranges and explicit out-of-range/invalid display policies
Original-normal displacement with declared drop/recompute normal policy, plus optional shared-prototype vector arrows
excluded: General field solvers, continuous-domain singularity proofs and unbounded adaptive sampling
Texture transfer functions, arbitrary shaders, lighting and full Blender node graph equivalence
Automatic field reevaluation on displaced vertices and implicit deformation feedback

upstream.role: Capturing field results makes their values belong to the produced geometry. Texloom uses explicit persistent names and immutable buffers, rather than importing Blender anonymous-attribute graph machinery.

license.note: Previously pinned conceptual source used by the mesh-field design. This feature independently implements its declared numerical contract; no source is copied or translated. Any later adaptation requires separate file-level license review.

upstream.role: Attribute domain is part of field evaluation context. Texloom exposes a small explicit transfer registry and does not silently perform every Blender domain adaptation.

inputs: An existing authored or upstream mesh, unique output resource ID, matching units and at least one scalar/vector expression
Read-only x/y/z/nx/ny/nz/index locals, source time and bounded shared parameters; an optional boolean mask
Explicit color stops, fixed/auto range, out-of-range behavior and invalid color; optional uniform displacement amplitude and arrow length scale
outputs: Unchanged raw finite values or explicit nulls, raw validity and presentation validity, and reported display range
An immutable derived mesh preserving topology; named linear-RGB vertex color and optional normal displacement
Optional instance sets share an authored arrow prototype and expose stable vertex identities, orientation, length and selection
Original declaration JSON and decoded scalar/vector/mask/amplitude/length-scale expressions are archived with spans
coordinates: All fields are evaluated on source mesh positions and source normals, before displacement
Colors interpolate in linear RGB; GPU output converts to display sRGB downstream
Displacement uses p + amplitude * rawScalar * sourceNormal; zero amplitude restores source geometry
Arrow local +X follows the vector; its explicit up vector and zero-vector policy resolve orientation
errorPolicy: Reject malformed or duplicate JSON, unknown fields, unsafe sidecars and capture budgets before publication
Reject source cycles, output collisions, mismatched units and unsupported expression types
Invalid field samples require explicit error or mask behavior; raw values are never replaced by clamped display values
Degenerate recomputed normals and zero vectors follow explicit policies rather than invented geometry

verification.command: python -m unittest tests.field_visualization_port_spec_test tests.field_visualization_capture_test tests.field_visualization_player_test -v; npm test
claims: The actual TeX example creates two spheres from one source: fixed-range color and color plus source-normal displacement
Independent browser arithmetic checks every raw scalar, mapped RGB, displaced point and exact resulting bounds
Independent camera/barycentric arithmetic checks visible GPU pixels after linear RGB interpolation and sRGB encoding
Reverse PNG captures, mobile amplitude controls, zero-amplitude geometry restoration and source immutability are checked
A separate real TeX fixture tests analytic vector-arrow directions, zero-vector hiding, invalid samples and auto-range behavior
notEstablished: Equivalence with the complete Blender field/node system
Correctness of the mathematical field between sampled vertices
Identical raster bytes across browsers or GPU drivers
General PDE integration, simulation state or lighting after displacement
